_meta: A list of items over which a closure (a small function) is created per item, used to show the late-binding closure trap: a function that refers to the loop variable captures the VARIABLE, not its value at the moment the function was created, so after the loop every closure sees the loop variable's FINAL value. items is the list looped over; the intent is to build one callback per item that returns its own item. The naive build -- a lambda that returns the loop variable directly -- makes all the closures share the one loop variable, so calling any of them returns the last item ('c'), never 'a' or 'b'. The fix binds the value at definition time by making it a default argument (lambda item=item: item): default arguments are evaluated once, when the function is defined, so each closure captures that iteration's value and the callbacks return their own items ('a','b','c'). This is not a bug in closures; it is the defined semantics of closing over a variable in a loop, and it appears in JavaScript (var), Python, and any language where loop closures capture by reference. items is the fixture; the naive and fixed closure results are computed by actually building and calling the closures.
